craft_claim: In Sanskrit poetics, resonance (dhvani) exceeds literal and figurative meaning, and sound, suggestion, and rasa co-produce sense, making sound a load-bearing part of meaning.

supporting_evidence.note: Anandavardhana establishes dhvani as the soul of poetry: suggested meaning outranks literal expression (abhidha) and metaphorical transfer (laksana).
Rasa-dhvani (suggested emotion) is ranked as the highest tier of poetic resonance, tying sound and suggestion to emotional effect.
Gerow documents the Sanskrit distinction between sound-figures and sense-figures, showing that sound-ornament is theorized as a meaning-bearing class, not mere decoration.

counterevidence.note: The doctrine was contested within Sanskrit poetics (the dhvani debates), and its technical vocabulary does not translate cleanly into English.

scope: Indian aesthetic theory and its descendants in South Asian literary practice.
exceptions: Technical instruction or didactic legal texts where ambiguity is harmful.
